name: Family reunification / family formation (partner)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires both partners being 18 or over.
This requires being married to, the registered partner of, or in a durable relationship with, a Dutch citizen or a person legally resident in the Netherlands.

value.note: gross SV-wage excl. holiday allowance, rate for Jan-Jun 2026; rises to €2,337.00 from 1 Jul 2026

requirements.blocker_text: This requires the sponsor to have independent, sufficient, and sustainable (12+ months) income of at least €2,294.40/month (excl. holiday allowance, Jan-Jun 2026 rate).
requirements.fix_path: Increase sponsor income to the required threshold and sustain it for 12+ months.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires passing the civic integration exam abroad (Basisexamen inburgering buitenland) at A1 level before an MVV is issued, unless exempt (under 18, state pension age, or a national of the EU/EEA, Australia, Canada, Japan, Monaco, New Zealand, Vatican, UK, US, South Korea, or Switzerland).
requirements.fix_path: Book and pass the 3-part exam (Knowledge of Dutch Society, Speaking, Reading) at the nearest embassy or consulate.

evidence_required.document: Marriage/registered partnership certificate or evidence of a durable relationship
Civic integration exam abroad pass certificate (unless exempt)
Sponsor's income evidence sustained over 12+ months

notes: Fee €254 adult / €85 child confirmed via IND. The civic integration exam abroad (A1, €150, paid to DUO) is a genuinely distinctive Dutch requirement not present on the equivalent UK or German family routes — worth surfacing as a real cross-country difference in a comparison view. Exemption list is broad (11 named nationalities plus age exemptions) and consequential, same pattern as Germany's A1-exemption list on the spouse route — many applicants likely qualify without realizing it. Income figure is LIVE-DUAL-DATED: €2,294.40 applies Jan-Jun 2026, rising to €2,337.00 from 1 Jul 2026 — this is the first route in the dataset to explicitly need a mid-year value change, distinct from the annual-only cadence seen in UK/Germany fee updates; flagged as a case that would benefit from the national-variables/formula mechanism if a future pass confirms the exact indexation link to the statutory minimum wage. citizenship_after_months (36) reflects the shorter naturalisation path available to spouses of Dutch citizens; a non-spouse durable-relationship partner would use the standard 60-month path instead — same class of within-route conditional variance flagged on other family routes across this dataset.
